n47d26c50dc3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Green Tribunal?
o: It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure
It follows the principles of natural justice
Its principal bench is at New Delhi
n47d26c50dc3.x: The NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it is guided by the principles of natural justice.

n80a7e5afdc9.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995, which never came into force, was repealed by the:
n80a7e5afdc9.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.

n1373765df4b.s: Under the Water and Air Acts, a 'Consent to Operate' from the State Pollution Control Board is needed before:
n1373765df4b.x: Consent to Operate is needed before production or discharge; Consent to Establish is needed before setting up the unit.

nae294988933.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rio Earth Summit, 1992 and its follow-ups?
o: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 as a Rio follow-up
The UNFCCC, CBD and UNCCD are the three Rio Conventions
The Forest Principles adopted at Rio are a legally binding convention
The UNFCCC and the CBD were opened for signature at Rio
nae294988933.x: The Forest Principles were a non-binding statement, not a legally binding convention.

n6bf1052ddd4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: It was opened for signature at the Stockholm Conference, 1972
Its Secretariat is located in Montreal, Canada
It is one of the three Rio Conventions
Its financial mechanism is the Global Environment Facility
n6bf1052ddd4.x: The CBD was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, not at Stockholm in 1972.

ne5ad5bc263b.s: Goal C of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework concerns:
o: Fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources
ne5ad5bc263b.x: Goal C concerns fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources; finance and technology is Goal D.

nd99c1779ff9.s: At CITES CoP20, the whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays were listed in:
nd99c1779ff9.x: Most sharks and rays are in Appendix II, but CoP20 listed the whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays in Appendix I.

n45bae8c886b.s: India's first accredited Wetland Cities under the Ramsar Convention (January 2025) are:
n45bae8c886b.x: Udaipur and Indore became India's first accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025.

ncedb314570f.s: How many Aichi Biodiversity Targets were set under the Strategic Plan 2011-2020?
ncedb314570f.x: There were 20 Aichi targets under five strategic goals; 23 is the number of KMGBF targets.

nd639f09b484.s: Which target of the Kunming-Montreal GBF seeks to halve global food waste by 2030?
nd639f09b484.x: Target 16 seeks to halve food waste; Target 6 concerns invasive alien species.

n5cc882d5692.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n5cc882d5692.x: World Environment Day on 5 June was an outcome of the Stockholm Conference, 1972, which also produced UNEP and a 26-principle Declaration.

n9cbb8f9cc93.s: In which year did India ratify the Nagoya Protocol?
n9cbb8f9cc93.x: India ratified the Nagoya Protocol in 2012; 2014 is the year the Protocol entered into force.

n2d87d3ad785.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Kunming-Montreal GBF is correctly matched?
o: Target 2 – Conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans
Target 16 – Cut invasive alien species by half
Target 18 – Mobilise US$200 billion a year
Target 22 – Full participation and rights of indigenous peoples and local communities
n2d87d3ad785.x: Target 22 concerns indigenous peoples and local communities; 30x30 is Target 3, invasive species Target 6 and US$200 billion Target 19.

na3d6cdc60cc.s: The principle that lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to postpone cost-effective measures against environmental harm is the:
na3d6cdc60cc.x: This is the precautionary principle; it does not allow preventive action to be postponed until full certainty.

n5d856c906b5.s: Which of the following was an outcome of the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development?
n5d856c906b5.x: The CBD, Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration and the UNFCCC came from Rio 1992; The Future We Want was the Rio+20 (2012) outcome.

nd9117d0d5c3.s: In the Sustainable Development Report 2025, India's rank in the SDG Index was:
nd9117d0d5c3.x: India ranked 99th out of 167 in SDR 2025, entering the top 100 for the first time.

nb40e1b67529.s: Which of the following runs counter to sustainable development?
o: Maximising economic growth at any cost
nb40e1b67529.x: Maximising growth at any cost conflicts with sustainable development, which balances economic, social and environmental concerns.

new.s: In which year was the Department of Environment created in India?
new.x: The Department of Environment was created in 1980; it became the Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985.

new.s: The Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) was formed in:
new.x: MoEF was formed in 1985, after the Department of Environment (1980); it was renamed MoEFCC in 2014.

new.s: The Central Pollution Control Board was originally constituted in 1974 under the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
new.x: CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.

new.s: The Central Pollution Control Board got its air-pollution functions from the:
new.x: Air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; the EPA 1986 only widened its scope.

new.s: The chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board is nominated by the:
new.x: CPCB is a statutory body under MoEFCC whose chairman is nominated by the Central Government.

new.s: The Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution was renamed the Central Pollution Control Board in:
new.x: The 1988 amendment renamed it the Central Pollution Control Board.

new.s: NAMP, run by the Central Pollution Control Board, stands for:
new.x: NAMP is the National Air Monitoring Programme of the CPCB, with real-time CAAQMS stations.

new.s: India's National Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched in:
new.x: The National AQI was launched in 2015 and gives daily AQI bulletins.

new.s: The head office of the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board is at:
new.x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada, with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

new.s: The chairperson of a State Pollution Control Board is nominated by the:
o: Governor on the advice of the NGT
new.x: An SPCB chair is nominated by the State Government; the CPCB chairman is nominated by the Central Government.

new.s: Apart from its head office, the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board has how many Regional offices?
new.x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

new.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
new.x: Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was the first NGT Chairperson; Justice Prakash Shrivastava is the current one.

new.s: Besides the Chairperson, the National Green Tribunal has Judicial and Expert Members numbering:
new.x: The NGT has a Chairperson with 10 to 20 Judicial and 10 to 20 Expert Members.

new.s: Which of the following is a circuit bench, not a zonal bench, of the National Green Tribunal?
new.x: Jodhpur, Shimla and Shillong are circuit benches; Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal benches.

new.s: The National Green Tribunal started functioning in:
new.x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010, the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and it started functioning in July 2011.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. Its zonal bench in western India is at Mumbai.
2. It aims to dispose of cases within 6 months.
3. It is a statutory, not a constitutional, body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; the zonal bench is at Pune, not Mumbai.

new.s: How many Acts are listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act, under the Tribunal's jurisdiction?
new.x: Seven Acts, from the Water Act 1974 to the Biological Diversity Act 2002, are in Schedule I.

new.s: Which of the following Acts is within the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
new.x: The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 is in Schedule I; the Wildlife Act 1972 and the Forest Rights Act 2006 are outside the NGT.

new.s: The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 was meant to hear:
new.x: The NEAA heard appeals against environmental clearances; strict liability for hazardous accidents was the NET Act 1995.

new.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, which regulates forest diversion, was enacted in:
new.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act is of 1980; the Wildlife Act is 1972 and the EPA 1986.

new.s: Under the Biological Diversity Act, a foreign entity seeking an IPR based on Indian biological resources must first obtain approval of the:
new.x: Foreigners need NBA approval to access bio-resources or traditional knowledge, and NBA approval precedes any IPR.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board, on NGT/MoEFCC direction, is developing biodiversity parks on the flood plains of:
new.x: The AP State Biodiversity Board is creating biodiversity parks on the flood plains of 5 polluted rivers.

new.s: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted in 1997 under:
new.x: The CGWA was set up in 1997 under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

new.s: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas was set up under an Act of:
new.x: The CAQM was set up under the CAQM Act 2021 and replaced the EPCA.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (AP SEIAA) clears which category of projects under the EIA Notification 2006?
new.x: AP SEIAA, constituted by MoEF order under Section 3 of the EPA, clears Category B projects.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Environment Management Corporation (APEMCL) was set up mainly for the disposal of:
new.x: APEMCL handles collection, transport, storage and disposal of industrial waste with APPCB, and is to expand to biomedical, battery and e-waste.

new.s: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is located at:
new.x: WII and the Forest Survey of India are both at Dehradun.

new.s: The Botanical Survey of India and the Zoological Survey of India are both headquartered at:
new.x: BSI and ZSI are both at Kolkata.

new.s: Which pair of institute and location is correctly matched?
new.x: GBPNIHE is at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora; IITR is at Lucknow, SACON at Coimbatore and NEERI at Nagpur.

new.s: Who was the only visiting head of government at the Stockholm Conference, 1972?
new.x: Indira Gandhi was the only visiting head of government at Stockholm; she linked poverty and environment.

new.s: The Stockholm Declaration of 1972 contained how many principles?
new.x: The Stockholm Declaration had 26 principles; the Rio Declaration of 1992 had 27.

new.s: World Environment Day was first observed in:
new.x: World Environment Day on 5 June came out of Stockholm 1972 and was first observed in 1973.

new.s: Rio+10, the World Summit on Sustainable Development of 2002, was held at:
new.x: Rio+10 (WSSD) was held at Johannesburg in 2002 and produced the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation.

new.s: The UN Environment Assembly (UNEA) was set up as an outcome of:
new.x: UNEA came from Rio+20 (2012); UNEP came from Stockholm 1972, though both are in Nairobi.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of obligations under the Ramsar Convention?
o: Banning all human use of wetlands
new.x: Ramsar's pillars are designation, wise use and international cooperation; wise use allows sustainable use.

new.s: As of 16 October 2026, how many Ramsar sites does India have?
new.x: India reached 101 sites with Glaw Lake and 103 on 16 October 2026 with Sukhna Lake and Sauj Jheel.

new.s: Kolleru Lake, Andhra Pradesh's only Ramsar site, was designated in:
new.x: Kolleru Lake, between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, was designated on 19 August 2002.

new.s: CITES entered into force on:
new.x: CITES was adopted on 3 March 1973 at Washington D.C. and entered into force on 1 July 1975.

new.s: The CITES Secretariat, administered by UNEP, is located at:
new.x: The CITES Secretariat is at Geneva; Gland hosts the Ramsar Secretariat.

new.s: World Wildlife Day, observed on 3 March, marks the signing of:
new.x: 3 March is the CITES signing day, proclaimed World Wildlife Day by the UNGA in 2013.

new.s: Under CITES, a species not necessarily threatened but which could become so without trade control is listed in:
new.x: Appendix II species may be traded with an export permit; Appendix I is for species threatened with extinction.

new.s: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, a statutory body under MoEFCC, was set up in:
new.x: The WCCB was set up in 2007 through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

new.s: India was removed from the CITES Review of Significant Trade for red sanders in:
new.x: India was under the Review of Significant Trade since 2004 and was removed at the 77th Standing Committee, Geneva, in November 2023.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus):
1. It is endemic to Seshachalam and the southern Eastern Ghats.
2. It is listed as Endangered by IUCN.
3. It is listed in CITES Appendix I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; red sanders is in CITES Appendix II, not Appendix I.

new.s: TRAFFIC, which works to ensure wildlife trade is not a threat to conservation, is a network of:
new.x: TRAFFIC (1976) is an NGO network of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IUCN?
o: It is a union of governments and NGOs
It is an organ of the United Nations
new.x: IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs, not a UN organ.

new.s: The Convention on Biological Diversity entered into force on:
new.x: The CBD text was adopted on 22 May 1992 and it entered into force on 29 December 1993.

new.s: India ratified the Convention on Biological Diversity in:
new.x: India ratified the CBD in 1994; the Biological Diversity Act followed in 2002.

new.s: The CBD COP hosted by India, COP11 in 2012, was held at:
new.x: CBD COP11 was held at Hyderabad in 2012.

new.s: Which pair of CBD COP and venue is correctly matched?
new.x: COP14 was at Sharm el-Sheikh; COP10 was Nagoya, COP12 Pyeongchang and COP16 Cali.

new.s: Under the Cartagena Protocol, the procedure required before the first transboundary movement of living modified organisms is the:
new.x: The Cartagena Protocol uses the advance informed agreement procedure; prior informed consent is a Nagoya pillar.

new.s: The Biosafety Clearing-House under the Cartagena Protocol is:
o: A laboratory for testing GM crops
An online platform for information on LMOs
new.x: The Biosafety Clearing-House is an online platform for LMO information, not a testing lab.

new.s: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of the Nagoya Protocol?
o: Traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources
new.x: The Nagoya Protocol covers plant, animal and microbial genetic resources and traditional knowledge, but excludes human genetic material.

new.s: Under India's three-tier biodiversity structure, People's Biodiversity Registers are prepared by the:
new.x: BMCs prepare People's Biodiversity Registers and can levy collection fees.

new.s: The online biodiversity information portal launched by the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board is:
new.x: AP State Biodiversity Board runs the BIOMIS and ABS End-to-End portals; PRANA is CPCB's NCAP portal.

new.s: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at:
new.x: The KMGBF was adopted at Montreal in December 2022, not at Kunming in 2021 or Cali in 2024.

new.s: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework has:
new.x: The KMGBF has 23 targets for 2030 and 4 goals for 2050; Aichi had 20 targets under 5 strategic goals.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Aichi Biodiversity Targets:
1. They were adopted at CBD COP10 at Nagoya in 2010.
2. Their deadline was 2030.
3. Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 found none of them fully met.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Aichi deadline was 2020, while the KMGBF targets run to 2030.

new.s: Target 6 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF seeks to cut the introduction and establishment of invasive alien species by at least:
new.x: Target 6 seeks a cut of at least 50% in invasive alien species.

new.s: India joined the High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People, whose goal is to protect 30% of land and ocean by 2030, as the first:
new.x: India joined on 7 October 2021 as the first BRICS country.

new.s: The High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People is co-chaired by:
o: Costa Rica, France and the UK
new.x: The Coalition is co-chaired by Costa Rica, France and the UK.

new.s: India released its updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030 at:
new.x: India's updated NBSAP with 23 national targets was released at COP16, Cali, in October 2024.

new.s: National reports to the Convention on Biological Diversity are submitted under:
new.x: National reports are submitted under Article 26, about every four years; Article 8(j) relates to indigenous peoples.

new.s: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is set up under the:
new.x: The GBF Fund is under the GEF.

new.s: The World Heritage Convention (1972) has its secretariat at:
new.x: The World Heritage Convention is a UNESCO convention with its secretariat at Paris; India ratified it in 1977.

new.s: Which pair of treaty and secretariat is correctly matched?
new.x: The IWC is at Cambridge, UK; UNCCD is at Bonn, the Ozone Secretariat at Nairobi and the Ramsar Secretariat at Gland.

new.s: When did India sign the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement)?
new.x: India signed the BBNJ Agreement in September 2024; ratification is under way. It entered into force on 17 January 2026.

new.s: World Wetlands Day, linked to the Ramsar Convention, is observed on:
new.x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February, the day the Ramsar Convention was signed in 1971.

new.s: The UN Decade on Biodiversity was declared for:
new.x: The UN Decade on Biodiversity is 2011-2020 (UNGA Res 65/161).

new.s: The Brundtland Commission, which produced 'Our Common Future', was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, then Prime Minister of:
new.x: Gro Harlem Brundtland was Prime Minister of Norway when she chaired the WCED.

new.s: The Brundtland Commission is formally known as the:
o: World Commission on Environment and Development
UN Conference on the Human Environment
new.x: The Brundtland Commission is the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), which published Our Common Future in 1987.

new.s: According to the Brundtland definition, sustainable development meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of:
o: Future generations to meet their own needs
new.x: The definition: development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

new.s: 'The Limits to Growth' (1972) was a report prepared for the:
new.x: The Limits to Growth was a report for the Club of Rome by an MIT team including Donella and Dennis Meadows.

new.s: The World Conservation Strategy of 1980 was launched by:
new.x: The World Conservation Strategy (1980) was launched by IUCN with UNEP and WWF.

new.s: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Our Common Future 2. Johannesburg Declaration 3. Stockholm Declaration 4. Rio Declaration
new.x: Stockholm Declaration 1972, Our Common Future 1987, Rio Declaration 1992, Johannesburg Declaration 2002.

new.s: Rio+5, the 1997 review of the Earth Summit, was held at:
new.x: Rio+5 was a UNGA special session in New York in 1997; Rio+10 was at Johannesburg in 2002.

new.s: The formal name of the 2002 Johannesburg summit (Rio+10) was the:
o: UN Conference on Environment and Development
new.x: Rio+10 was the World Summit on Sustainable Development (WSSD); UNCSD was Rio+20 in 2012.

new.s: The 2030 Agenda's Sustainable Development Goals have how many targets?
new.x: There are 17 SDGs, 169 targets and 232 indicators.

new.s: The Millennium Development Goals, which preceded the SDGs, covered the period:
new.x: The MDGs ran from 2000 to 2015, followed by the SDGs from 2016.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an environmental-protection issue in the classic sense?
new.x: Poverty alleviation is a social issue; climate change, pollution, degradation and resource depletion are environmental-protection issues.

new.s: The principle of carrying capacity in sustainable development means:
o: The polluter bears the cost of pollution control
Human use must stay within what ecosystems can support
new.x: Carrying capacity means using resources within what ecosystems can support; the other options describe CBDR, polluter pays and precaution.

new.s: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of sustainable development?
o: Growth that runs down natural capital
new.x: Sustainable development includes present needs, equity and inclusion, but excludes growth that runs down natural capital.

new.s: Earth Overshoot Day was conceived by:
new.x: Earth Overshoot Day was conceived by Andrew Simms of the New Economics Foundation, UK; the first campaign was in 2006.

new.s: The ecological footprint is measured in:
new.x: The ecological footprint is the productive land and sea needed to meet consumption and absorb wastes, measured in global hectares.

new.s: Which case is associated with the polluter-pays principle in India, alongside the Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
new.x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996) applied the polluter-pays principle.

new.s: The Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India judgment, which made sustainable development part of Indian law, was delivered in:
new.x: The Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum case was decided in 1996.

new.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 is organised around how many 'Sutras'?
new.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 has Ten Sutras, aiming at a Wealthy, Healthy and Happy Andhra Pradesh.
